newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov't says May trade balance will be better.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't says May trade balance will be better.

text.p: The Brazilian government expects May to show a better trade balance than April's $951 million deficit, a wider gap than most analysts had expected last month, officials said.

Mauricio Cortes, secretary for foreign trade at the Ministry of Industry and Commerce, and Rui Modenesi, deputy secretary for economic policy at the Finance Ministry, said recent measures taken to slow imports and boost exports would help the result.
"We will already have this month conditions even more favourable than in the past month," Cortes told reporters.

Modenesi said a recent increase in the so-called IOF tax on credit purchases would reduce demand for imported consumer goods and last year's exemption of commodities and semi-manufactured goods from export tax would continue to boost overseas sales.
Recent restrictions on import financing would also help, he said.
"In relation to the trade balance, there is no motive for concern," he said.
April's gap exceeded market expectations for a $750 million deficit, according to a Reuters survey.
